speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
title: O Be Wise
session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

points.text: President D. Todd Christofferson spoke about “O Be Wise”.

quotes.text: Today I feel a bit like the Book of Mormon prophet Jacob, when he felt compelled by the Spirit to address subjects that were not particularly edifying, having to use “boldness of speech,” as he put it, instead of feasting on “the pleasing word of God.” So, with a sense of duty, I turn to the subject of gambling.
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Putting money or something of value at risk to bet on a particular outcome or event is an activity that has plagued mankind almost, I suppose, from the beginning of time. And time has not made it any more worthwhile or any less harmful. Unfortunately, in recent years, gambling has become incredibly pervasive.
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: The growth in worldwide gambling is primarily driven by three new online markets. First is online sports betting, which involves wagers on sports scores, statistics, or events. Second is online casino-type games, sometimes referred to as internet or iGaming: slot games, roulette, blackjack, poker, and so on. A third, relatively new platform is what are called “prediction markets” that allow participants to bet on whether something will or will not happen and when. It could be tied to anything: interest rates, elections, sports, wildfires, or even, if you can imagine, the timing of the Second Coming. (Where would you go to collect on that bet?)
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: In the United States, 36 percent of boys age 11 to 17 reported gambling last year, rising from 32 percent at age 11 to 49 percent—virtually half of all boys—at age 17. Equally troubling is the substantial percentage of 18- to 29-year-old women who now participate in gambling each year, especially mobile sports betting, slots, and lotteries.
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Earlier this year a prominent journalist wrote in The Atlantic magazine about his preplanned, monthslong experience with sports gambling. Among other things, he noted: “Experts estimate that only about 2 to 5 percent of gamblers will develop compulsive behaviors. But … that small percentage becomes a very large number when tens of millions of [people] suddenly have casinos in their pockets.”
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: Perhaps you think your character and your commitment to divine covenants are sufficiently strong that, for you, wagers would never become more than occasional, casual fun. Maybe. But whether you are right about that or not, have you considered how your example might affect others?
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: If your moral standing is secure, then undoubtedly there are others who look to you as a guide for upright living. That would certainly be true for your children but also others that you may or may not know who are watching and learning from what they see in you. They may be newer or weaker in the faith. A little gambling that seemingly has only a minor impact in your life may be more costly to them if they take license from your example.
quotes.speaker: President D. Todd Christofferson
quotes.session: Saturday Morning Session, October 2026 General Conference

quotes.text: “For if any man see thee which hast knowledge [of the gospel] sit at meat in the idol’s temple, shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols;
